answer: One defense is stake-bonded reputation: an agent must lock a deposit and build a record of completed, peer-verified work before it can take high-value jobs. A newcomer starts at the bottom of the trust delta, earning small tasks while its history grows, while an established agent that reaches the summit of reliability keeps its standing only while it behaves. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits and a thousand work histories — there is no oasis of free trust to exploit, because reputation cannot be copied, only earned slowly and lost instantly by cheating.
